questions.q: What is the name of the central point on a number line that separates positive and negative numbers?
questions.a: The central point is called zero (0). A wrong answer suggests the student has not yet internalized the reference point of the number system.

questions.q: If you have two numbers, -3 and -7, which one is further to the right on the number line, and why?
questions.a: -3 is further to the right because it is greater than -7. A student who says -7 is greater shows they are treating negative numbers like positive numbers, ignoring the leftward direction of negative value.

questions.q: Plot the integers -4, 2, and 0 on a number line and list them in increasing order.
questions.a: The order is -4, 0, 2. A student who lists them as 2, 0, -4 is failing to recognize that "increasing" means moving from the smallest (leftmost) to the largest (rightmost) value.

questions.q: Compare the position of 5 and -5 on the number line. Are they the same distance from zero?
questions.a: Yes, they are the same distance from zero in opposite directions. A wrong answer suggests the student does not understand that positive and negative integers are symmetrical reflections across the zero point.

questions.q: If an elevator is at -2 and moves 3 units to the right, where does it end up?
questions.a: It ends at +1. A student answering -5 indicates they are moving the wrong direction (left) instead of the positive direction (right).

questions.q: Draw a number line and show where -6 and -1 are. If you were a person walking from -6 toward -1, would you be moving toward a larger or smaller number?
questions.a: You would be moving toward a larger number. An answer of "smaller" shows the student is misled by the digit size (6 vs 1) rather than the actual position on the line.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A number line is a straight line that ______ integers as points at equal distances from a center point called zero; numbers to the right are positive, and numbers to the left are negative.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are ______ in an elevator in a building with underground parking.
Fill in the blank: To understand the number line, draw a horizontal line and place ______ in the center.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to correctly plot any given integer on a number line and use the position of numbers to compare their values (e.g., identifying that -5 is smaller than -2).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are standing in an elevator in a building with ______ parking.
